items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
TSD-TRP-26-002, Integrated Mobility Plan – Project Outline
notes:
Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, provided an introduction to the presentation. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. Mike Henderson, Director, Transportation Services, provided further information on the Integrated Mobility Plan and public engagement conducted.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner indicated that accessibility legislation does give design specifications, but that engagement reveals that sometimes more is necessary. He further added that illumination work is continually being done with an update expected for the end of 2026 or early 2027.

Responding to questions, M. Henderson indicated that this plan and associated guidelines would apply to roads in the next 10 years in need of repair and maintenance in addition to new roads. He further spoke to snow removal and maintenance on regional roads as a sign that communication and collaboration with area municipalities is critical. D. Spooner indicated that there are working groups including area municipalities but that this could be looked at.

In response to questions, M. Henderson spoke to challenges with rural design and on-street parking, as well as the option for pedestrians and cyclist on both sides of the road where possible. He added that the plan will be context-specific.

Replying to questions, D. Spooner explained that there are a number of projects anticipated for beyond 2041, that are going to be reviewed and see what items are to be displaced. Furthermore, D. Spooner indicated that the Mio Vision gives data on intersections and allows for predictability, thus potentially leading to the ability to service area municipalities. He added that a full cycling network within the Region is a goal, and staff are also looking at winter cycling enhancements as well.

Received for information.

items.title: EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Acting CAO, provided an introduction to the presentation. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. Nicole Sapeta, Senior Engineer (Water), provided information on the Region's water supply system and water capacity constraints for the Mannheim service area, verified by a third-party, Agile Infrastructure. N. Sapeta spoke to the revised methodology for reviewing groundwater supply and the introduction of minimum operational resiliency targets.

Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, provided information on the upcoming developments and the water services available for new developments. He elaborated on the impacts to development, including the inability to enter into new servicing agreements, and confirmed the Region has not asked area municipalities to halt existing building permits or withhold new permits.

Amy Shaw, Director, Water and Wastewater Operations, indicated staff need to review ministerial guidelines and recommendations to determine if new servicing is required. She elaborated on the work being done to resolve the water capacity issues, including repairs to infrastructure and optimization of existing sources, as well as looking at new projects to add net-new supply capacities.

In reply to a question from the Committee, M. Goetzke indicated there is a whole water team that works on efficiency with large water users.

Replying to questions, M. Goetzke clarified the uses of the methodologies for tracking water capacity which are compliant with associated guidelines. A. Shaw spoke to support from the ministry of the environment who indicated the methodologies can be changed as system owner, provided they are technically sound and protective of drinking water system. Furthermore, N. Sapeta answered that the peer-reviewed report provides information as to the effects of the recommendations, including the 20% proposed operating buffer. N. Sapeta indicated the constraint for Mannheim is limited to the Integrated Urban System (IUS).

In response to questions, A. Shaw indicated that staff have set up internal technical working group, which is being expanded to include industry experts and area municipality technical staff.

Responding to questions, R. Regier answered that it is correct that issued but unbuilt permits are accounted for, and that builders approved in 2024 can go ahead with their building. M. Goetzke explained it is not a full picture, and there are still some concerns about capacity. R. Regier indicated the Region is not providing comments and not advising area municipalities. He added that school boards have not been met with, but that staff are planning to engage with them, including universities and colleges.

In reply to questions, A. Shaw indicated that one solution will not solve the issue, but actions are planned for improvement such as getting water plants back up to full capacity pending design approvals.

In response to questions, M. Goetzke provided that a confluence of factors led to the current issues. N. Sapeta added that staff undertook a comprehensive analysis with multiple pieces coming together to come to the realization of the issue.

Replying to questions, Connie MacDonald, Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications, provided clarity on the approach to media partners to communicate the water capacity issue. She indicated that due to technical nature of the problem, staff wanted to give media time to get in-depth understanding, acknowledging media partners have varying needs. N. Sapeta added there has been ongoing data sharing.

Wayne Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, clarified status of reserves related to water.

In reply to questions, N. Sapeta answered that the operational resiliency buffer change being proposed that the system is showing stress now, so the longer it stays at increased strain level, the higher the risk. A. Shaw clarified that if we do not increase the operational resiliency, we cannot take things offline, to be able to take things offline for repairs, thus, the need higher operational resiliency.

Julien Bell, P.Eng., Vice President of Agile Infrastructure, provided more clarity on the operational resiliency. N. Sapeta added that staff are looking more broadly as well through the water supply strategy update.

In response to questions, M. Goetzke indicated that data can be packaged to area municipalities, however, before sharing with the public, legal would need to review the information for freedom of information considerations. A. Shaw confirmed the data can be distributed within a week or two.

Responding to questions, M. Goetzke indicated that staff can bring preliminary list of projects to be completed, but stressed that the list will not be a vetted list. He added that staff are also talking with ministry of environment to fast-track of projects, so the list will not adequately consider timeline and costs. A. Shaw further added that there are risks with it not being complete, due to it being based on a lot of tentative information.

The amendment "That Regional Council is provided the preliminary list in advance of the release to the public at least 48 hours in advance" was adopted with unanimous consent.

In reply to a question from the Committee, A. Shaw spoke to water taking permits and information that staff is privy to, indicating this information is mostly within the jurisdiction of the province.

Responding to questions, W. Steffler clarified how additional consultant fees are being addressed through the budget.

motions.item_title: EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
motions.text: Whereas in late November 2025, through on-going work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot and Whereas a Technical Team has been meeting and working diligently since that time to research, understand and address these infrastructure challenges, and Whereas the Region of Waterloo staff on an ongoing basis monitors, maintains and updates an annual Asset Management Plan and Master Plans for all regional information including regional water and wastewater infrastructure and Whereas the Asset Management Plan “describes the replacement value and physical condition of the Region’ s asset portfolio” and this information is utilized to predict when renewals and repairs will likely be needed’, and Whereas the 2025 Asset Management Plan includes an Asset Condition profile of Water and Wastewater Services (see Appendix A, Figure A.1 of that report), Levels of Service information, a Drinking Water Quality Management System, Expenditure Forecasts and other aspects of the system all of which are all designed and used to ‘…manage risk to the water supply system by identifying possible hazards, assigning risk scores and identifying procedures, process objectives and preventative measures to help assess and mitigate risk to the environment.” and Whereas housing and employment developments currently in progress and scheduled to begin or to be completed in 2026 and developments being planned within the next 5 years require information as soon as possible regarding the short, medium and long-term plans for repairing the regional water and wastewater infrastructure, Whereas although the Report EES-WAS-26-001indicates that “a more fulsome impact of the capacity issue to the 2026 operating and capital budget is anticipated to be available late Q1 2026”, there is pressing need for area municipalities and the development community to understand the repairs needed and the timelines involved, Therefore be it resolved that the timeline for a preliminary list of the short, medium and long-term plans for the necessary infrastructure repairs be made publicly available before the end of January 2026 rather than in late Q1 2026.
motions.text_html:
Whereas in late November 2025, through on-going work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot and
Whereas a Technical Team has been meeting and working diligently since that time to research, understand and address these infrastructure challenges, and
Whereas the Region of Waterloo staff on an ongoing basis monitors, maintains and updates an annual Asset Management Plan and Master Plans for all regional information including regional water and wastewater infrastructure and
Whereas the Asset Management Plan “describes the replacement value and physical condition of the Region’ s asset portfolio” and this information is utilized to predict when renewals and repairs will likely be needed’, and 
Whereas the 2025 Asset Management Plan includes an Asset Condition profile of Water and Wastewater Services (see Appendix A, Figure A.1 of that report), Levels of Service information, a Drinking Water Quality Management System, Expenditure Forecasts and other aspects of the system all of which are all designed and used to ‘…manage risk to the water supply system by identifying possible hazards, assigning risk scores and identifying procedures, process objectives and preventative measures to help assess and mitigate risk to the environment.” and 
Whereas housing and employment developments currently in progress and scheduled to begin or to be completed in 2026 and developments being planned within the next 5 years require information as soon as possible regarding the short, medium and long-term plans for repairing the regional water and wastewater infrastructure,
Whereas although the Report EES-WAS-26-001indicates that “a more fulsome impact of the capacity issue to the 2026 operating and capital budget is anticipated to be available late Q1 2026”, there is pressing need for area municipalities and the development community to understand the repairs needed and the timelines involved, 
Therefore be it resolved that the timeline for a preliminary list of the short, medium and long-term plans for the necessary infrastructure repairs be made publicly available before the end of January 2026 rather than in late Q1 2026.

motions.item_title: EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
motions.text: Whereas in late November 2025, through on-going work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot and Whereas a Technical Team has been meeting and working diligently since that time to research, understand and address these infrastructure challenges, and Whereas the Report EES-WAS-26-001indicates that ‘…several factors and observations led technical staff to reassess how remaining water capacity was being monitored including “a plateauing of conservation efforts…” and Whereas the water conservation efforts referred to in the report do not include the breadth of water conservation opportunities available to municipalities, homeowners, businesses, property owners, property managers and property developers which include but are not limited to, for example, natural assets – more trees, native plants, floodplain protection – the installation of green infrastructure, the adoption of greywater systems, rainwater capture for personal watering, smart irrigation systems, models for more sustainable water practices and an understanding of how technology and smart metering and data analytics can increase water conservation, and Whereas municipalities like the Region of Waterloo and other municipalities including area municipalities have the opportunity to provide leadership and direction with robust water conservation policy(ies) and appropriate regulations to support water conservation efforts, and Whereas water conservation efforts are required in tandem with the necessary infrastructure repairs and sourcing of new wells in order to ensure a robust water supply now and in the future, Therefore Be It Resolved that staff are directed to report back by the end of Q2 June 2026 with water conservation policy options for the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Committee’s and Regional Council’s consideration and Further that input from relevant community partners including but not limited to Reep Green Solutions, Sustainable Waterloo Region, Build Urban, the Waterloo Region Homebuilders Association, the Grand River Conservation Authority, Grand River Environmental Network and area municipalities is sought and included in the water conservation policy options proposed.
motions.text_html:
Whereas in late November 2025, through on-going work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot and
Whereas a Technical Team has been meeting and working diligently since that time to research, understand and address these infrastructure challenges, and
Whereas the Report EES-WAS-26-001indicates that ‘…several factors and observations led technical staff to reassess how remaining water capacity was being monitored including “a plateauing of conservation efforts…” and
Whereas the water conservation efforts referred to in the report do not include the breadth of water conservation opportunities available to municipalities, homeowners, businesses, property owners, property managers and property developers which include but are not limited to, for example, natural assets – more trees, native plants, floodplain protection – the installation of green infrastructure, the adoption of greywater systems, rainwater capture for personal watering, smart irrigation systems, models for more sustainable water practices and an understanding of how technology and smart metering and data analytics can increase water conservation, and
Whereas municipalities like the Region of Waterloo and other municipalities including area municipalities have the opportunity to provide leadership and direction with robust water conservation policy(ies) and appropriate regulations to support water conservation efforts, and
Whereas water conservation efforts are required in tandem with the necessary infrastructure repairs and sourcing of new wells in order to ensure a robust water supply now and in the future, 
Therefore Be It Resolved that staff are directed to report back by the end of Q2 June 2026 with water conservation policy options for the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Committee’s and Regional Council’s consideration and
Further that input from relevant community partners including but not limited to Reep Green Solutions, Sustainable Waterloo Region, Build Urban, the Waterloo Region Homebuilders Association, the Grand River Conservation Authority, Grand River Environmental Network and area municipalities is sought and included in the water conservation policy options proposed.

motions.item_title: EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
motions.text: THAT Regional staff be directed to provide a clear written definition of what activities are currently paused or restricted, including but not limited to servicing agreements, allocations, registrations, redevelopment scenarios, and planning approvals, no later than 12:00 p.m. on Friday, January 16, 2026, to: Regional Council, Area Municipal Councils, and the public; AND THAT Regional staff be further directed to report back to Council no later than Feb. 10, 2026 with a decision-ready information package related to the Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint, including: a) updated water supply and demand calculations using the revised methodology, including key assumptions and sensitivity testing under multiple resiliency buffer scenarios; b) a summary of interim operational and/or engineering measures considered to mitigate capacity constraints, including feasibility, estimated costs, regulatory requirements, and indicative timelines; c) an update of how the Region intends to address and resolve water supply capacity constraints while respecting the planning authority of Area Municipalities, including: how Regional water and wastewater infrastructure planning, investment, and operational decisions will support Area Municipalities in carrying out their legislated land use planning responsibilities; how growth-related servicing decisions will be aligned with approved Area Municipal official plans and provincial planning policy, rather than used as a mechanism to direct or prioritize growth outcomes; and what actions the Region will take, within its jurisdiction, to address system capacity and reliability so that Area Municipalities are able to proceed with planning and development in accordance with provincial legislation; d) a detailed workplan identifying specific dates and milestones, rather than quarter-based timelines, for further analysis, decisions, and recommendations requiring Council consideration; e) clear identification of matters requiring Council direction versus those within administrative authority. AND FURTHER THAT Regional staff be directed to bring forward a communications plan that includes public messaging, stakeholder outreach plans, or external communications related to the Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint for Council review and approval in advance of release or implementation, recognizing that: the matter has significant policy, economic, growth, and inter-municipal implications; such communications reflect Council direction and Council accountability; and this issue extends beyond routine administrative communications.
motions.text_html:
THAT Regional staff be directed to provide a clear written definition of what activities are currently paused or restricted, including but not limited to servicing agreements, allocations, registrations, redevelopment scenarios, and planning approvals, no later than 12:00 p.m. on Friday, January 16, 2026, to:

  • Regional Council,
  • Area Municipal Councils, and
  • the public;

AND THAT Regional staff be further directed to report back to Council no later than Feb. 10, 2026 with a decision-ready information package related to the Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint, including:
a) updated water supply and demand calculations using the revised methodology, including key assumptions and sensitivity testing under multiple resiliency buffer scenarios;
b) a summary of interim operational and/or engineering measures considered to mitigate capacity constraints, including feasibility, estimated costs, regulatory requirements, and indicative timelines;
c) an update of how the Region intends to address and resolve water supply capacity constraints while respecting the planning authority of Area Municipalities, including:

  • how Regional water and wastewater infrastructure planning, investment, and operational decisions will support Area Municipalities in carrying out their legislated land use planning responsibilities;
  • how growth-related servicing decisions will be aligned with approved Area Municipal official plans and provincial planning policy, rather than used as a mechanism to direct or prioritize growth outcomes; and
  • what actions the Region will take, within its jurisdiction, to address system capacity and reliability so that Area Municipalities are able to proceed with planning and development in accordance with provincial legislation;

d) a detailed workplan identifying specific dates and milestones, rather than quarter-based timelines, for further analysis, decisions, and recommendations requiring Council consideration;
e) clear identification of matters requiring Council direction versus those within administrative authority.

AND FURTHER THAT Regional staff be directed to bring forward a communications plan that includes public messaging, stakeholder outreach plans, or external communications related to the Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint for Council review and approval in advance of release or implementation, recognizing that:

  • the matter has significant policy, economic, growth, and inter-municipal implications;
  • such communications reflect Council direction and Council accountability; and
  • this issue extends beyond routine administrative communications.

motions.item_title: EES-WAS-26-001, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint Update
motions.text: * Withdrew via unanimous consent * THAT Regional staff be directed to prepare an inventory and impact assessment of active and pending Ontario Permits to Take Water (PTTWs) that draw from groundwater sources within the Region of Waterloo and/or from connected aquifers within the broader watershed, including those located outside Regional boundaries; AND THAT the assessment include: a) the purpose, permitted volumes, and term of each identified permit; b) the relationship, if any, between those takings and Regional municipal water supply systems, including the Mannheim Service Area; c) an assessment of cumulative impacts on groundwater availability using the Region’s revised water capacity methodology; and d) identification of any permits that may warrant enhanced scrutiny, mitigation measures, or engagement with the Province in order to protect municipal drinking water security; AND THAT staff report back in open session by end of Q2 2026 with findings and recommended next steps, including potential advocacy or coordination with the Province of Ontario.
motions.text_html:
* Withdrew via unanimous consent *

THAT Regional staff be directed to prepare an inventory and impact assessment of active and pending Ontario Permits to Take Water (PTTWs) that draw from groundwater sources within the Region of Waterloo and/or from connected aquifers within the broader watershed, including those located outside Regional boundaries;

AND THAT the assessment include:

  1. a) the purpose, permitted volumes, and term of each identified permit;
  2. b) the relationship, if any, between those takings and Regional municipal water supply systems, including the Mannheim Service Area;
  3. c) an assessment of cumulative impacts on groundwater availability using the Region’s revised water capacity methodology; and
  4. d) identification of any permits that may warrant enhanced scrutiny, mitigation measures, or engagement with the Province in order to protect municipal drinking water security;

AND THAT staff report back in open session by end of Q2 2026 with findings and recommended next steps, including potential advocacy or coordination with the Province of Ontario.

motions.item_title: Councillor M. Rodrigues, Re: Road Safety Program
motions.text: WHEREAS the Road User Safety Program provides comprehensive, evidence-based solutions to reduce serious injuries and fatalities on Regional Roads, with an emphasis on reducing serious collisions involving vulnerable road users including in school zones; WHEREAS revenues from Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) in school zones would have funded the Road Safety Reserve as a primary funding source for the Road User Safety Program; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional staff report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee by Q2 2026 and following wind-down of the ASE program to: Establish how to allocate the remaining Road Safety Reserve balance to fund school zone road safety initiatives starting in 2026; and Provide options on how to fund the Road Safety Reserve in future years, including but not limited to sources from transportation user fees and redlight camera revenues.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the Road User Safety Program provides comprehensive, evidence-based solutions to reduce serious injuries and fatalities on Regional Roads, with an emphasis on reducing serious collisions involving vulnerable road users including in school zones;

WHEREAS revenues from Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) in school zones would have funded the Road Safety Reserve as a primary funding source for the Road User Safety Program;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional staff report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee by Q2 2026 and following wind-down of the ASE program to:

  1. Establish how to allocate the remaining Road Safety Reserve balance to fund school zone road safety initiatives starting in 2026; and
  2. Provide options on how to fund the Road Safety Reserve in future years, including but not limited to sources from transportation user fees and redlight camera revenues.
